description: Approved Peanut runtime and container image lanes (PAR-505). A lane is a program decision recorded in the parity tracker's Decision Log, not a dependency update — so Renovate surfaces lane changes for an explicit human decision instead of opening them as routine PRs.

packageRules.description: Node and npm: the lane is major 22 LTS. Crossing it is a fleet decision (parity Decision Log, 2026-08-13). Surface on the dependency dashboard; never open or auto-merge silently.

PHP, MariaDB and ClickHouse: the lane is pinned at MINOR granularity (PHP 8.4, MariaDB 11.4 LTS, ClickHouse 25.12), so a minor bump already leaves the approved lane. PHP 8.4 is the Laravel lane (PAR-202); MariaDB 11.4 is the default server-backed transactional lane (PAR-302).

MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO: the lane is pinned at MAJOR granularity. MySQL 8 is a time-bounded compatibility exception (PAR-302); PostgreSQL 16/17 and the Langfuse stack are architecture-specific exceptions (PAR-209, PAR-302).

Keep every Node declaration moving together. Repositories now cross-check engines.node, packageManager, .nvmrc, CI setup-node and container base images in a fail-closed runtime contract, so a bump that lands in only one of them turns CI red. Grouping them into one branch is what makes an in-lane Node update mergeable at all.
Same reasoning for PHP: composer config.platform, CI php-version and the container base image are cross-checked, so in-lane PHP patches must move as one branch.

Never auto-merge a container image digest. Digest-pinned images are the immutability contract for production-classified stacks (PAR-209), and the approved rollout for changing one requires snapshot, canary and rollback that a dependency bot cannot perform. The update is still raised — it just needs a person.
